title: Make brightness scale (linear or perceptual) and minimum value configurable per-device by the user
line: Advanced Power Settings now lets you switch the built-in screen to perceptual brightness steps and raise its lowest backlight level, saved per backlight device.
explanation: Powerdevil passes brightness to the laptop backlight linearly and always uses raw value 1 as the lowest level. On panels whose luminance is linear in the raw value (like the reporter's nvidia_wmi_ec_backlight), the lowest steps are huge and the top ones barely visible, and some panels go dark at raw 1; this can't be detected reliably, which is why automatic perceptual mapping (powerdevil!134) never landed. The change adds two per-device settings in powerdevilrc ([Backlight][<device>]: PerceptualBrightness, MinimumBrightness) shown under a new "Built-in Screen Brightness" section of Advanced Power Settings; the daemon maps Plasma's brightness onto the raw range from the chosen minimum to the maximum, optionally on a CIE L*-style curve, applies changes immediately, and the defaults keep the exact current 1:1 mapping.

commits.message:
backlight: let users pick a perceptual scale and minimum brightness

Some backlights change luminance linearly, so the lowest steps are huge
and the highest barely visible, and some turn off before the lowest raw
value. Advanced Power Settings now offers both settings per device.

BUG: 528781

media.caption: Advanced Power Settings on master: nothing about the screen backlight
With the change and a backlight present: new "Built-in Screen Brightness" section with the perceptual scale checkbox, the minimum level, and their help texts
Master's BacklightBrightness on a fake 800-level nvidia_wmi_ec_backlight: raw value always equals the requested value, lowest is raw 1
Same device with perceptual steps and minimum 4: low slider levels are finely spread, the lowest level is raw 4, 50% is raw 156 (about half perceived brightness)
